videos.script: A wall socket in a meeting room is a live port on a switch. Whoever plugs in gets the whole network. {{socket}} 802.1X changes that. The port stays shut until the machine proves who it is, and a server it trusts says yes. {{parties}} In this lesson a company laptop presents its certificate and the port opens for it alone. {{open}} A visitor's machine offers a certificate it signed itself, and then borrows the laptop's address. Both stay outside. {{refused}} And every port that opens leaves a line saying who was there, which is useful, and personal. {{log}}
